part_1_engineering_technical_brief.audience: Firmware, Motor Controls, and Systems Engineering Teams

firmware_analysis.enforcement_location: Main application loop of motor controller firmware (MCU: STM32F405, branch: main-v3.x) [cite: 508-509]
enforcement_points: safety_monitor.c: Secondary hard-cutoff check with 5% margin [cite: 513]

motor_controller_parameters.pid_velocity_loop: Increase Kp to ~0.50; decrease Ki to ~0.014 to prevent integral windup [cite: 536-537]
motor_controller_parameters.thermal_constraints: 10 mph ceiling requires max phase current of 42A; requires PCB trace thermal verification [cite: 532-533]

hardware_implications.gear_ratio: Current 14.5:1 ratio provides adequate margin for 10 mph; limiting factor is motor thermal capacity [cite: 573-576]
hardware_implications.battery_management: BMS continuous discharge limit may require increase to 30A for 10 mph builds [cite: 592]

braking_system.projections: Likely failure at 10 mph (3.6–4.2m projected vs 3.5m internal limit) [cite: 602]
braking_system.required_action: 10 mph release requires hardware upgrade (rotor diameter increase, dual-circuit braking, or regen torque limit increase) [cite: 603]

estimated_performance_impact.range_reduction: ~30% reduction at 8 mph; ~50% reduction at 10 mph [cite: 587]

strategic_urgency.sales_performance: Missed revenue targets for three consecutive quarters; 61% of lost opportunities cite low maximum speed [cite: 659-661]
strategic_urgency.market_demand: 74% of current users prefer higher speed options [cite: 670]
strategic_urgency.regulatory_status: Recent updates explicitly permit higher speed ceilings for this category [cite: 672]

part_2_business_and_marketing_rationale.competitive_risk: Three competitors launched 8–10 mph variants in last 14 months; institutional buyers are standardizing on 8 mph minimums [cite: 679-687]

commercial_strategy.phased_launch: Align launch with Engineering Phase 2 (8 mph) in months 4–6; do not wait for 10 mph validation [cite: 726-727]
commercial_strategy.pricing: 8–12% price premium recommended for 8 mph tier; 10 mph positioned as premium performance SKU [cite: 732-733]
messaging_guidelines: Frame as capability expansion, not a 'fix' for old models [cite: 696-720]
Be transparent about range reduction to manage expectations [cite: 722-723]
Emphasize regulatory alignment for institutional and clinical confidence [cite: 703-717]

conclusion: The market has moved toward 8–10 mph standards. The business case for moving quickly on 8 mph while proceeding deliberately on 10 mph is strong, as inaction poses a greater risk than execution[cite: 740].
